title: Place-Based Rural Infrastructure Investment in Kazakhstan: Short-Run District Effects and Later Descriptive Trends of the Auyl–El Besigi Programme
content: Evidence on place-based rural investment from resource-dependent, post-socialist and fiscally centralised economies is scarce. We assess Kazakhstan's Auyl–El Besigi programme, which financed infrastructure in selected villages in 2019–2025. Programme exposure was reconstructed from 1106 final amended budget decisions for the main sample of 135 rural districts, drawn from a broader collection of 1298 distinct decisions for 2019–2026, and linked to official statistics and Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS) night-time lights. Callaway–Sant'Anna difference-in-differences estimates against not-yet-funded districts cover a window ending in 2021 (2022 as a robustness check); later years are analysed descriptively. Early-funded districts had about twice the rural population of later entrants. After covariate adjustment, short-run estimates are small and imprecise: 0.021 log points for night-time light (95% confidence interval −0.035 to 0.076) and 0.008 for average wages (−0.006 to 0.022). No robust short-run district-level effect was detectable using the available administrative and satellite indicators. Trends to 2024–2025 are similar across entry groups, and larger recorded allocations coincide descriptively with faster wage growth. The findings highlight a broader evaluation problem for centrally financed place-based programmes in data-constrained institutional settings: without settlement-level project, expenditure and service-quality records, economically meaningful local effects may remain undetectable in aggregate administrative data.
